newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker, RGI call off merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Aker, RGI call off merger talk.

text.p: Norwegian engineering and offshore group Aker ASA said on Monday it was no longer considering a merger with investment group Resource Group International (RGI) following talks at the weekend.

In a statement to the Oslo bourse, Aker said the board had concluded that a fusion between the two company's would have made sense strategically but the two parties could not agree on the exchange value of their shares.
"Negotiations have made it clear that the distance concerning the exchange ratio is too wide for there to be a basis to continue the talks," the statement said.
Trawler-based RGI earlier this year acquired 30 percent of Aker shares and has options to buy nearly 10 percent more.
In a separate statement, RGI said it had been positive about a deal with Aker but the proposed terms of a share exchange precluded further talks.
"As a main shareholder RGI will continue to be an active long-term owner in Aker," RGI said.
Aker said it would continue to consider other options for future growth.
Shareholders have already agreed to a merger of Aker's Oil and Gas Technology division and Maritime Group to form a new company, Aker Maritime ASA, of which Aker will hold an 80 percent stake.
